content.tldr: Iceberg supports two row-level deletion formats: Positional Deletes reference exact file paths and row offsets, while Equality Deletes filter rows by matching column values.
content.simple_explanation: In Merge-on-Read (MoR) tables, deleting rows without rewriting entire Parquet files requires writing delete files. A Positional Delete file explicitly lists `(file_path, row_position)` pairs pointing to rows that must be ignored during scans. An Equality Delete file stores specific column values (e.g. `id = 1042`), instructing the reader to discard any row matching that value. Positional deletes are fast for readers to evaluate, while equality deletes are faster for streaming ingestion to write.
content.real_world_example: Canceling appointments in a physical ledger: a positional delete puts a red line through 'page 4, line 12'; an equality delete places a note on the front desk saying 'cancel any appointment booked under the name Smith'.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Equality deletes require query readers to perform expensive broadcast hash joins at scan time to filter deleted rows. High-throughput analytic tables should compact equality deletes into positional deletes or rewrite data files via compaction.
